main_text.p: L.ille aut ille, 25. de legat. lib. tertio, scribit, cum in uerbis nulla ambiguitas eft, uolun-tatis quæstionem admitti nõ debere. Quo ex loco perspi-cuè intelligimus, uoluntatis quæstionem dici à Paulo ex uerbis nasci: & tum demum exiftere, cum in uerbis eft am-biguitas. ubi tamè pinguius, ut paulo antè dixi, uerba pro scripto posuit. In singulis igi-tur hisce capitibus ac fonti-bus generales quædam regu-læ latent, nondum perscri-ptæ illæ quidem ac peruulga-tæ, sed in hominum mentib. atq; ingenijs quasi notiones quedã anticipatę & infitę, ad quas

page.notes: Right margin: a handwritten ink annotation in a later hand (several lines of cursive, partly Greek-looking), not printed text, so not transcribed. Faint pencil-like marks and stray strokes at the lower left and centre (around the foot of the page) are not printed text. A small mark at the lower left may be a gathering signature, but it is too faint to read, so no signature is given. Printed text uses long s rendered as s throughout; "quedã" and "tamè" carry tildes as printed.
